108.tells: Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ Al-Kawthar, which means a lot of good. So we say thank you by praying and giving to Allah alone. The person who said the Prophet's name would be forgotten was the one who was cut off.
prophet: One day the Prophet ﷺ was with his friends and he smiled. He told them a new surah had just come down, and he read this surah. Then he asked, 'Do you know what Al-Kawthar is?' He said: 'It is a river that my Lord promised me. It has a lot of good in it. It is also a pond where my followers will come on the Day of Judgment. Its cups are as many as the stars in the sky.' (Told by Anas, in Sahih Muslim.)

The Prophet ﷺ also told about the night he went up to the heavens. He said he came to a river with domes of hollow pearl on its banks. He asked Jibril, 'What is this?' Jibril said, 'This is Al-Kawthar.' (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, from Anas.)
scholars: Ibn Abbas said: 'Al-Kawthar is the good that Allah gave to the Prophet.' (Sahih al-Bukhari.) Someone told Sa'id ibn Jubayr that people say it is a river in Paradise. Sa'id said, 'The river in Paradise is part of the good that Allah gave him.'

Ibn Kathir explains it like this: Allah gave you so much good in this life and the next. So pray, and make your sacrifice only for your Lord. Worship Him alone. When you sacrifice an animal, say only Allah's name.

Ibn Kathir says they thought that when the Prophet's sons died, his name would be forgotten. That was wrong! Allah kept his name remembered all over the world, and people will follow his teaching until the Day of Gathering.

103.tells: Time is going by. Every person is losing, except people who believe, do good things, tell each other to follow the truth, and tell each other to be patient.
scholars: Ibn Kathir explains: Allah makes an exception. People who believe in their hearts and do good things with their bodies are not in loss.
Ibn Kathir writes that when two of the Prophet's friends met, they did not part until one of them had read Surah Al-Asr to the other, and they had said salaam to each other. (At-Tabarani.)
The great scholar Ash-Shafi'i said: 'If people thought deeply about this surah, it would be enough for them.' (Told by Ibn Kathir.)

112.tells: Allah is One. Everyone needs Him, and He needs no one. He has no child and no parent, and nothing is like Him.
prophet: The idol worshippers once said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'Muhammad, tell us about the family of your Lord.' Then Allah sent down this surah. (Ahmad and At-Tirmidhi, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b.)

The Prophet ﷺ said this surah is worth a third of the Quran. A man had heard another man read 'Say: He is Allah, One' again and again, and he thought it was a small thing. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'By the One who holds my soul in His hand, it is equal to a third of the Quran.' (Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Sa'id.)

Aisha told about a man the Prophet ﷺ sent with an army. He always ended his prayer by reading this surah. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'Ask him why he does that.' The man said, 'Because it tells about Ar-Rahman, and I love to read it.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Tell him that Allah loves him.' (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.)

A man from the Ansar led the prayer in the mosque of Quba. He read this surah in every rakah, and then another surah. His friends told him to stop, but he said he loved it. The Prophet ﷺ told him: 'Your love for it will take you to Paradise.' (Sahih al-Bukhari.)

The Prophet ﷺ taught his friend to say 'Say: He is Allah, One' and the two surahs of safety, Al-Falaq and An-Nas, three times in the evening and three times in the morning. He said: 'They will be enough for you.' (Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi and An-Nasa'i. At-Tirmidhi said hasan sahih gharib.)

Aisha said that every night when the Prophet ﷺ went to bed, he put his hands together and blew into them. Then he read Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas into them. Then he wiped his body with his hands, starting with his head and face. He did this three times. (Sahih al-Bukhari.)
scholars: Ikrimah said that different people believed different things. The Jews said, 'We worship Uzayr, the son of Allah.' The Christians said, 'We worship the Messiah, the son of Allah.' The fire worshippers said, 'We worship the sun and the moon.' The idol worshippers said, 'We worship idols.' So Allah told His Messenger ﷺ to say: 'He is Allah, One.' (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
Ibn Kathir explains that 'Ahad' (One) means the only One. He has no equal, no helper, and nothing is like Him. This word can only be used for Allah, because He is perfect in everything about Him.
Ibn Abbas said As-Samad means the One that all of creation needs for everything they need and ask for. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)

106.tells: Allah kept the Quraysh safe and fed them. So they should say thank you and worship the Lord of this House.
scholars: Ibn Kathir says this surah is linked to Surah Al-Fil, the one before it. Allah stopped the elephant army and destroyed it, so the Quraysh could stay together safely in their city. (Muhammad ibn Ishaq and Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd said this.) The word 'ilaf' means joining them together.

Ibn Kathir explains: every winter they traveled to Yemen, and every summer they traveled to Ash-Sham, to trade. They came back safe, because people respected them as the people who lived near Allah's holy place. Even people who traveled with them were safe.

Ibn Kathir explains: Allah feeds them when they are hungry and keeps them safe from fear. So they should worship Him alone and not idols. Whoever listens, Allah gives safety in this life and the next. Whoever does not listen, Allah takes both away. (Ibn Kathir also shows Surah An-Nahl, 16:112–113, about a safe town that said no to Allah's favors, so Allah made it taste hunger and fear.)

110.tells: When Allah helps you win, do not be proud. Say thank you, praise Allah and ask Him to forgive you. Allah accepts people who come back to Him.
prophet: Ibn Abbas said this is the last whole surah that came down to the Prophet ﷺ. (An-Nasa'i, told by Ibn Kathir.)
When this surah came down, the Prophet ﷺ said, 'My death has been announced to me.' He passed away that same year. (Ahmad, from Ibn Abbas.)

Aisha said the Prophet ﷺ often said when he bowed and when he put his head down in prayer: 'Glory to You, our Lord, and praise to You. O Allah, forgive me.' He was following what the Quran told him. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says 'the help of Allah and the Conquest' means the day Makkah was opened to the Muslims. Before that, many tribes of Arabia waited. They said, 'If Muhammad wins over his own people, then he is a true prophet.'

Ibn Abbas, Umar and others: some older men at Badr only thought it meant 'thank Allah when you win.' Ibn Abbas told Umar it was a sign that the Prophet's life was almost done. Umar said, 'I know nothing about it other than what you said.' (Sahih al-Bukhari.)
Ibn Kathir says that less than two years after Makkah was opened, all of Arabia had become Muslim. Every tribe said they believed.
Ibn Kathir explains: when you get a big win, do not be proud. Say thank you to Allah, and ask Him to forgive you. Allah accepts people who come back to Him.

114.tells: We ask the Lord, the King and the God of all people to keep us safe from the whisperer who hides when we remember Allah.
prophet: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Did you see the ayahs that came down tonight? Nothing like them was ever seen.' They are 'Say: I seek safety with the Lord of the Falaq' and 'Say: I seek safety with the Lord of the people.' (Sahih Muslim, from Uqbah.)

The Prophet ﷺ told his friend Uqbah that no one asks Allah for protection with anything like Al-Falaq and An-Nas. (An-Nasa'i.) He also said they are among the best two surahs people read. (Ahmad, Abu Dawud, An-Nasa'i.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says three names of Allah are in this surah: Lord, King and God. Allah is the Lord of everything, the King of everything and the God of everything.

Ibn Abbas said: the whisperer who hides is the shaytan who sits on the heart of a person. When the person forgets, he whispers. When the person remembers Allah, he runs away. Mujahid and Qatadah said the same. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
Ibn Kathir ends his book with this surah: 'All praise and thanks are due to Allah, the Lord of all that exists.'

105.tells: Abrahah came with a huge army to knock down the Kaaba. Allah stopped them with small birds. No one can take down the House of Allah when Allah protects it.
prophet: At Al-Hudaybiyyah the Prophet's camel, Al-Qaswa, sat down and would not go on. People said she was stubborn. The Prophet ﷺ said she was not stubborn. She was stopped by the One who stopped the elephant from Makkah. (Sahih al-Bukhari.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says this is a favor Allah did for the Quraysh. He saved them from the people of the elephant who wanted to knock down the Kaaba and wipe out every sign of it.

Ibn Kathir tells the story. Abrahah was a governor of Yemen for the king of Ethiopia. He built a huge church in Sana'a and wanted the Arabs to go there for pilgrimage instead of the Kaaba. The Arabs said no. Then a man from the Quraysh went and made it dirty at night. (Some say young men set it on fire.) So Abrahah promised to destroy the Kaaba stone by stone.
Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was born in the same year, according to the most known opinion.
Ibn Kathir (telling Ibn Ishaq) says Allah sent birds from the sea, like swallows. The word 'ababil' means birds in groups.
Ibn Kathir says later the Prophet ﷺ reminded the Quraysh about this as a favor from Allah. Because of it, they could stay safely in their city. Surah Quraysh comes next to remind them.

111.tells: Abu Lahab was an uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, and he hurt him. His money and his children did not save him.
prophet: One day the Prophet ﷺ climbed a small hill and called the Quraysh. When they came together, he asked, 'If I told you an enemy would come at morning or evening, would you believe me?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'I am warning you before a very hard punishment.' Abu Lahab said: 'You gathered us for this? May you be ruined!' Then Allah sent down this surah. (Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn Abbas.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says Abu Lahab was an uncle of the Prophet ﷺ. His real name was Abdul-Uzza. People called him Abu Lahab because his face was so bright, like fire. He hurt the Prophet ﷺ a lot.
Ibn Mas'ud said Abu Lahab said, 'If what my nephew says is true, I will save myself from the punishment with my money and my children.' So Allah sent this ayah. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
Ibn Kathir says his wife was Umm Jamil. Her name was Arwa, a daughter of Harb, and the sister of Abu Sufyan. She helped her husband in not believing and in being stubborn.

113.tells: We ask the Lord of the morning to keep us safe from bad things: the evil in what He made, the dark night, magic and a jealous person.
prophet: The Prophet ﷺ taught his friend Uqbah this surah and An-Nas and said: 'Read them every time you go to sleep and every time you get up.' (Abu Dawud and An-Nasa'i.)

The Prophet ﷺ asked a man, 'Should I tell you the best thing people use to ask for safety?' Then he said it was 'Say: I seek safety with the Lord of Al-Falaq' and 'Say: I seek safety with the Lord of the people.' (An-Nasa'i.)
Aisha said that when the Prophet ﷺ was sick, he read these two surahs over himself and blew. When his pain got worse, Aisha read them and wiped his hand over him. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Malik.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says Jabir, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and many others said Al-Falaq is the morning. It is like where Allah says He splits the daybreak.
Ibn Kathir says this means from every bad thing in everything Allah made. Al-Hasan al-Basri said it means things like Hell and Iblis.
Ibn Kathir says 'ghasiq' means night when it comes with darkness. Mujahid said 'when it waqab' means when the sun goes down.

107.tells: Do you know who says no to the Day of Payback? The one who is mean to orphans, does not help the poor, is careless about prayer, shows off, and will not help others.
prophet: The Prophet ﷺ said three times: 'This is the prayer of the hypocrite.' He sits and watches the sun until it is almost setting. Then he stands and pecks four rakahs like a bird, and hardly remembers Allah in them. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, told by Ibn Kathir.)
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever tells people about his good deed so they will hear it, Allah will make it known to people, and make him small.' (Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn Amr.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says 'Ad-Din' here means the Next Life and the Payback on the Last Day.
Ibn Kathir says this person is mean to the orphan. He does not give him what he has a right to. He does not feed him or treat him kindly.
Ibn Abbas and others said this means the people who pretend. They pray when people can see them, but do not pray when alone. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)

Ibn Kathir says 'sahun' can mean they do not pray at all, or they pray after the time is over (Masruq and Abu Ad-Duha), or they always wait until the very end of the time, or they do not pray it the right way, or they are not paying attention to its meaning.
Ibn Mas'ud said 'Al-Ma'un' is what people give each other, like an axe, a pot, a bucket and things like that. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
